battle.name: 莫多克戰爭
battle.brief: 一八七二至七三年，莫多克人拒絕遷入克拉馬特保留地，退到加州與俄勒岡邊境的華納山天然堡壘；美軍以步兵第四、六團為主圍攻四月，靠山地榴彈砲與掘壕逼近才迫其屈服。鐵甲艦代表的正是同一個十年海軍裝甲化的轉折，與堡壘「小砲打不穿」的道理相通。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 交戰一方是莫多克人。莫多克屬高原語族肖展語支的一支部族，原居加州東北部、俄勒岡南部與內華達東北部的高原湖盆，散居數千人的社群，以弓矢、矛與戰棍為主；一八六四年條約把他們逐入圖萊湖的克拉馬特保留地，與克拉馬特人共用土地而只分得極小一份，此後不斷有族人逃回山區，到一八七二年秋仍留在保留地的莫多克人不足百人，這批人拒絕受克拉馬特人管轄，也不接受美方另行配給地塊的安排。另一方是美國西部部隊：骨幹為步兵第四團（駐沃太華堡）與第六團的分遣連，配騎兵第一團、第二團的偵察分隊，另有工兵、醫療與通信人員，後來有加利福尼亞與俄勒岡的民兵志願隊加入，砲隊由團屬砲與山地榴彈砲組成，指揮上屬國防部太平洋戰區，戰區司令為最高統帥，遠征軍指揮官在前線統一調度，印第安事務局的保留地經理則是文書上的中央一方。保留地內部另有交涉管道，克拉馬特首長與美軍哨所之間往來文書不斷。莫多克一方沒有常設指揮部，進入堡壘的三百人左右靠火堆會議議事，卡普坦·傑克是事實上的領袖，重大決策由首領會議一致通過，作戰單位則以家族與個人追隨關係臨時組成。
countriesEn: One belligerent was the Modoc people. The Modoc were a branch of the Shastan group within the Plateau languages, originally inhabiting the plateaux and lake basins of northeastern California, southern Oregon and northeastern Nevada in communities numbering several thousand, and armed mainly with the bow, the lance and the war club. The treaties of 1864 drove them into the Klamath Reservation at Tule Lake, where they were made to share the land with the Klamath and received only a very small allotment of their own, and from then on Modoc kept escaping back into the mountains, so that by the autumn of 1872 fewer than a hundred remained on the reservation. Those who stayed refused to accept the authority of the Klamath and equally refused the arrangement by which the United States proposed to allot them separate land. The other belligerent was the United States Army in the West. Its backbone was detachments of the 4th Infantry, then at Fort Vancouver, and of the 6th Infantry, with scout detachments from the 1st and 2nd Cavalry, together with engineers, medical and signal personnel; California and Oregon militia volunteers were added later, and the artillery consisted of regimental guns and mountain howitzers. The chain of command ran through the War Department's Department of the Pacific, with the department commander as the supreme authority and an expedition commander unifying operations on the line, while the reservation agent of the Indian Office was the central party on paper. Inside the reservation there was a separate channel of negotiation, with constant correspondence between Klamath headmen and the army posts. The Modoc side had no standing command structure. The three hundred or so people who took up position in the stronghold did their council around campfires; Captain Jack was the leader in practice, major decisions were taken by a council of headmen reached by consensus, and tactical units were put together on the fly out of family ties and personal followership.
people: 莫多克一方，卡普坦·傑克（Kintpuash）是全場的樞紐。他出身莫多克有勢力的家族，父親老傑克是部族中最有威望的長者之一，他本人則以「上尉」之名在首領會議中代表族中一支，受到族人擁戴。傑克據守華納山堡壘四個月，主導了對美軍巡邏的還擊、對糧道的襲擾，最後在突圍時率殘部離開堡壘，被追兵擊斃於山路。他的父親老傑克、首領「三人」（Three Children）、捲髮頭目（Curleyhead）與戰首斯克拉洛姆（Scralom）同樣是關鍵人物：捲髮頭目在四月的堡壘攻擊首日陣亡，斯克拉洛姆通曉數種語言並能直接與美軍交涉，老傑克與三人代表莫多克在六月初接受了美軍的投降條件，其後老傑克在突圍中被自己人誤殺，另有十歲的查理（Ten-year-old Charlie）死在同一夜的追殺裡。另一邊，太平洋戰區司令布里格adier將軍愛德華·坎比（Edward R. S. Canby）於一八七三年一月二十六日的洛斯特里弗之役中被莫多克狙擊陣亡，是美方陣亡的最高級指揮員，戰區指揮由此一度中斷，遠征軍指揮官接手把圍城維持到底。軍醫約翰·埃爾斯沃思（Doc Ellsworth）是唯一能與莫多克直接交涉的白人，被莫多克人稱為「瘋子吉姆」，他屢次走出堡壘談判，最後促成六月一日的投降。騎兵第一團的奧蒙德上尉（Ormond）於一八七二年十一月二十九日率巡邏隊進入堡壘一帶，遭莫多克伏擊而損失慘重。步兵第四團的史丹利上尉（David S. Stanley）在洛斯特里弗之役率部作戰，事後獲國會授勳。克拉馬特族的嚮導黑吉姆（Black Jim）替美軍追蹤莫多克，最後被莫多克人殺害。華盛頓的戰爭部與總統府始終在追問進度，印第安事務局則擔心莫多克人與克拉馬特人合流，遠征軍的後方因此沒有穩定的政策可以依靠。
peopleEn: On the Modoc side Captain Jack, Kintpuash, was the pivot of the whole affair. He came from a family of standing among the Modoc, his father Old Jack being one of the most respected elders of the tribe, and he himself represented one of the lineages in the council of headmen under the name of captain, and was held in esteem by the people. Jack held the stronghold in the Warner Mountains for four months, directing the counter-stroke against an American patrol, the harassment of the supply columns, and finally the break-out from the stronghold, after which he was killed on the mountain road by the pursuing troops. His father Old Jack, the headman called Three Children, the war chief Curleyhead and the war chief Scralom were likewise key figures. Curleyhead fell on the first day of the assault on the stronghold in April; Scralom spoke several languages and could parley directly with the Americans; Old Jack and Three Children spoke for the Modoc when the surrender terms were accepted in early June, after which Old Jack was shot by his own people during the break-out, and a boy of ten, Ten-year-old Charlie, was killed in the same night's pursuit. On the other side, Brigadier General Edward R. S. Canby, commander of the Department of the Pacific, was shot dead by Modoc marksmen at the action of the Lost River on 26 January 1873, the highest ranking American officer to fall in the field, and the chain of command in the department broke for a time before an expedition commander took over and carried the siege through to the end. John Ellsworth, an assistant surgeon, was the only white man who could negotiate directly with the Modoc, whom they called Crazy Jim; he walked out of the stronghold again and again to talk and finally brought about the surrender of 1 June. Captain Ormond of the 1st Cavalry led the patrol that entered the neighbourhood of the stronghold on 29 November 1872 and was badly cut up in the ensuing ambush. Captain David S. Stanley of the 4th Infantry led his company in the action of the Lost River and was afterwards honoured by Congress. Black Jim, a Klamath guide, tracked the Modoc for the Americans and was finally killed by them. In Washington the War Department and the executive house kept asking after progress, the Indian Office worried that the Modoc and the Klamath might combine, and the expedition in the field had no settled policy behind it to lean on.
kits: 卡面這件鐵甲艦在莫多克戰爭裡是一張年代卡。英國海軍一八六二年的鐵甲艦把木殼包上鐵皮，裝甲第一次厚到能擋住實心彈，砲位與砲門的佈置從此只能繞著裝甲的形狀安排，這個轉折正是同期海軍技術的標誌。若要在這場戰爭的戰場上找一件與鐵甲艦同構的東西，那就是莫多克人選的天然堡壘：華納山的岩壁、巨石與松林替他們裝上了天然護甲，步槍與後膛槍打上去只留白痕，小口徑砲打不穿岩體，於是美軍的砲兵設計只能環繞岩體迂迴——先以山地榴彈砲消滅堡內的糧食、馬匹與通道，再由工兵在砲火下掘壕逼近，這與當年海軍面對裝甲時「先想辦法再打穿」的路子是同一種思路。實際交火中，美軍步兵配一八六六年型與一八七〇年型斯普林菲爾德五〇口径後膛步槍（.50-70），另有.44-40亨利式與.44-70陷阱式步槍，騎兵用一八七〇年型加特林手槍與左輪手槍，砲兵配一八六四年型山地榴彈砲與十二磅野戰榴彈砲，砲車由騾與牛牽引，軍中同時攜帶軍犬搜尋山徑。莫多克人則以自製複合弓、長箭、矛與戰棍為主力，也使用從居民與保留地取得的前膛步槍與手槍；堡內的胸牆由倒木、散石與削頂的松樹殘幹堆成，彈坑依岩壁挖出，另有取水的小溪、馬廄與存放穀物的棚屋。太平洋沿岸的軍需與兵員輸送仍靠蒸汽郵船與軍用運輸船，鐵甲艦代表的正是同一個十年海軍裝甲化的轉折。
kitsEn: The ironclad on this card is an era marker for the Modoc War. The British ironclads of 1862 sheathed a wooden hull in iron, and armour was for the first time thick enough to keep out a solid shot, so the disposition of guns and gunports had thereafter to be arranged around the shape of the armour; that turning point is the emblem of naval technology in the same decade. If one looks for something in this war on the battlefield that is structurally the same thing as an ironclad, it is the natural stronghold the Modoc chose. The rock walls, boulders and pine forest of the Warner Mountains gave them armour of their own; rifles and breach-loading carbines struck the rock and left nothing but marks, light guns could not penetrate the rock face, and the American artillery therefore had to work its way around the obstacle: mountain howitzers first to destroy the food, the horses and the passages inside, then engineers digging a sap forward under fire. That is precisely the logic the navy applied when it met armour, find a way round before you find a way through. In the actual shooting, the American infantry carried 1866 and 1870 pattern Springfield .50 calibre breech-loading rifles (.50-70), with .44-40 Henry and .44-70 trapdoor carbines; the cavalry used the 1870 pattern Gatling pistol and revolvers; the artillery had 1864 pattern mountain howitzers and twelve-pounder field howitzers, the guns hauled by mules and oxen; and the army took dogs with it to work the mountain tracks. The Modoc fought with their own composite bows, long arrows, lances and war clubs, and also used old muzzle-loading muskets and pistols taken from settlers and from the reservation. Their breastworks inside the stronghold were built of fallen timber, loose rock and the stumps of topped pines, their firing pits were cut into the rock face, and they had a small stream for water, a horse barn and a shed for stored grain. Along the Pacific coast, transport of men and supplies still ran on steamships and military transports, and the ironclad stands for the armouring of the navy in that very decade.
tactics: 莫多克人的整套戰術可以概括成一句話：不打曠野決戰，把美軍拖進自己選的地形。十一月廿九日，巡邏隊進入華納山南部的山谷後被莫多克以弓矢與步槍伏擊，傷亡慘重；此後他們佔據天然岩堡，憑岩壁與灌木構成的射擊孔居高臨下，專挑美軍單獨巡邏、糧車與汲水的小隊下手，夜里摸出堡壘取水取糧，天亮前退回。美軍這邊沿用一八七〇年代遠征的標準做法：以騎兵搜索寬正面，以步兵分連縱隊佔領山嶺與峽口，夜間宿營設柵，圍城期間以山地榴彈砲日以繼夜地射擊岩縫與堡內通道，同時派工兵小組在夜裡掘壕，一點一點把壕溝掘進射程之內，再以狙擊手壓制對方的射擊孔。一八七三年四月十一日的總攻是最不講究的一次：美軍把加利福尼亞與俄勒岡的民兵志願隊排在第一線，前面是清障部隊與擲彈筒手，後面才是步兵與砲兵，此舉在國內輿論上受到尖銳批評。攻堅失敗後圍城延續到六月，其間美軍屢次搜索周邊山谷，摧毀耕地、畜群與藏糧。六月六日夜，殘部趁暴雨衝出堡壘，渡過深溝、翻越岩脊往北逃竄，軍犬與嚮導在後緊追，追兵在無遮蔽的峽谷中追上突圍隊伍，戰鬥多在近距離內以步槍與刺刀解決。糧秣方面，全靠自沃太華堡經喀斯喀特山脈、斯內克河谷運到前線的騾隊與馬車輸送，山道狹窄，冬季有冰雪封路之虞，這是遠征軍最難解決的問題。
tacticsEn: The whole of the Modoc tactic can be put in one sentence: no set-piece battle in the open, drag the Americans into terrain of your own choosing. On 29 November a patrol that entered the valleys south of the Warner Mountains was ambushed with arrows and musket fire and cut to pieces. After that the Modoc held the natural rock fortress, shooting down from firing holes cut in the rock and masked with brush, and they went specifically after American patrols, supply wagons and small water parties, slipping out at night for water and food and returning before daylight. The Americans on their side followed the standard practice of the expeditions of the 1870s: cavalry searching a broad front, infantry in company columns taking the ridges and the mouths of the canyons, picketed camp lines at night, and during the siege mountain howitzers firing day and night into the clefts in the rock and into the passages of the stronghold, while engineer parties dug forward at night, inch by inch, until the trench was inside range, and sharpshooters covered the enemy's firing holes. The general assault of 11 April 1873 was the least carefully managed of all: the American command put California and Oregon militia volunteers in the first line, with a pioneer detachment and grenadiers in front of them and the infantry and guns behind, a measure that drew sharp criticism in the press at home. After the assault failed the siege dragged on into June, with repeated searches of the surrounding valleys and the destruction of fields, herds and hidden stores of food. On the night of 6 June the remnant broke out of the stronghold in a rainstorm, crossed the ravines and climbed the ridges heading north, with the army dogs and the guides in close pursuit; the pursuers caught the runaways in a canyon without cover, and the fighting was settled at close range with rifle and bayonet. Supply came entirely by mule train and wagon from Fort Vancouver, over the Cascades and down the Snake river valley to the front, on tracks narrow enough to be a problem in themselves, with ice and snow liable to close them in winter, and that was the difficulty the expedition could least solve.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。戰爭爆發時仍留在保留地的莫多克人不足一百人，此前逃入山區者另計；一八七三年三月進入堡壘者約三百人，其中能持槍作戰者五六十人，另有婦孺，重要取水點與馬廄設在堡外數百碼處。美軍方面，一八七二年十一月二十九日第一次接觸的巡邏隊約六十人；一八七三年一月二十六日洛斯特里弗之役的出擊部隊三四百人，坎比陣亡，美軍陣亡六人左右、受傷近三十人，莫多克亦有數人陣亡；四月十一日總攻的出動兵力在六百人上下，其中民兵志願隊佔相當比例，美軍陣亡七人、受傷五十餘人，莫多克損失無從確切統計，僅知堡內土木在砲擊中被逐段摧毀。圍城自一八七三年一月底延續到六月一日，凡約四個月，砲擊用山地榴彈砲數門，陣亡的將校除坎比外另有數人。關鍵日期依序為：1872年11月29日首次接觸、1873年1月26日洛斯特里弗之役、1873年3月美軍抵達並建立砲兵陣地、1873年4月11日起的堡壘總攻、1873年6月1日莫多克方面同意投降、1873年6月6日夜突圍與十歲查理之死、1873年6月30日卡普坦·傑克在追捕中被擊斃、1873年10月三名被軍法審判定罪的莫多克人被執行死刑，餘眾則被遷往印第安領地。遠征軍自沃太華堡翻越喀斯喀特山脈至華納山，行程數百英里，補給靠騾隊與馬車輸送。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. At the outbreak fewer than a hundred Modoc remained on the reservation, those who had already fled into the mountains being counted separately; by March 1873 about three hundred people had taken up position in the stronghold, of whom fifty or sixty were able to bear arms, the rest being women and children, and the important water point and the horse barn lay several hundred yards outside the works. On the American side, the patrol that first came into contact on 29 November 1872 numbered about sixty men; the column that attacked at the Lost River on 26 January 1873 numbered three to four hundred, Canby was killed, the Americans lost about six dead and close to thirty wounded, and a few Modoc were also killed; the force committed in the assault of 11 April numbered in the region of six hundred, a substantial proportion of them militia volunteers, with seven Americans dead and some fifty wounded, while the Modoc losses cannot be established and it is known only that the works inside the stronghold were destroyed piecemeal by the bombardment. The siege ran from the end of January 1873 to 1 June, roughly four months, with several mountain howitzers in action, and other officers besides Canby were killed. The key dates in order are: 29 November 1872, first contact; 26 January 1873, the action of the Lost River; March 1873, the American arrival and the establishment of the battery; 11 April 1873, the assault on the stronghold; 1 June 1873, the Modoc agreement to surrender; the night of 6 June 1873, the break-out and the death of Ten-year-old Charlie; 30 June 1873, the death of Captain Jack in the pursuit; October 1873, the execution of three Modoc condemned by a military commission, the remainder of the prisoners being removed to Indian Territory. The expedition covered several hundred miles from Fort Vancouver, over the Cascades, to the Warner Mountains, with supplies carried by mule train and wagon.
cause: 打起來有幾層原因。最深的一層是土地：一八六四年之後，條約把莫多克人的原居地割讓出去，把他們塞進圖萊湖的克拉馬特保留地，與克拉馬特人共用一片地，分給莫多克人的份額極小；族人多年間因欠債與私酒交易逐步失地，向拓殖者購地也屢屢受阻，申訴不果。第二層是保留地內的權力分配：莫多克人不接受受克拉馬特首長管轄，要求獨立的土地配給；印第安事務局的經理既要聽命於華盛頓，又要避免把人放跑，於是把要求一拖再拖。第三層是錢與物資：美方承諾的津貼與賠償物資並未按時足額送到，有一批運貨在途中被劫或因天候耽擱而失落，族人拿到手的數目遠低於所期。第四層是暴力接觸：保留地內不斷有衝突，士兵巡邏與莫多克人互相開槍，傷者與死者累積；美軍曾以追查治安為名要求莫多克首領到哨所報到而遭拒絕，也曾以拘押為名收走幾名族人，怨氣越積越深。直接導火線是一八七二年十一月的一場遭遇：美軍巡邏在圖萊湖一帶追查失竊與失物，與莫多克人正面交火，雙方都有傷亡，莫多克人隨即退入華納山，佔據天然堡壘，零星衝突於是變成一場圍城。
causeEn: There were several layers of cause behind the fighting. The deepest was land. After 1864 the treaties ceded the Modoc homelands and packed them into the Klamath Reservation at Tule Lake, to be put on a parcel shared with the Klamath and to receive a very small share of their own. Through the years the tribe lost land to debt and to the liquor trade, purchases from the settlers were repeatedly blocked, and their complaints produced nothing. The second layer was the distribution of authority inside the reservation. The Modoc would not accept the authority of the Klamath headmen and asked for an allotment of their own; the reservation agent had to obey Washington while also trying to prevent the people from running away, and so the request was put off again and again. The third layer was money and goods. The allowances and compensation promised to the tribe were not delivered on time or in full; one consignment was robbed on the road or lost to weather, and what the people actually received was far below what had been promised. The fourth layer was violent contact. Skirmishes inside the reservation were constant, patrols and Modoc shot at one another, and the wounded and the dead accumulated. The army demanded that Modoc headmen report to the posts on grounds of public order and was refused, and it also took several people into custody on a pretext, which deepened the resentment. The immediate spark was an encounter in November 1872. An American patrol in the neighbourhood of Tule Lake was following up thefts and missing property, met the Modoc face to face, and there was shooting on both sides with casualties on both sides. The Modoc then withdrew into the Warner Mountains and occupied the natural stronghold, and a series of clashes became a siege.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果遠出戰場之外。莫多克人作為一個獨立的族群就此告終：留在保留地的百餘人被拆散遷往內陸的克拉馬特聚落，突圍後被俘與零散投降的數十人被送往印第安領地的夸帕威保留地，與堪薩斯、俄克拉何馬的族群混居，語言與習俗在幾代人裡散失；華納山的家園則被併入聯邦林地。克拉馬特人連帶受損：戰後被嚴格限制在保留地內，未經許可不得離開，並被要求隨身攜帶辨識標記，其保留地面積在隨後十數年裡不斷被削減，測量界線一退再退。作戰方法上，這是美國陸軍最後幾次「遠征、圍城、清剿」式印第安戰爭之一，砲兵壓制、工兵掘壕、志願隊頂在第一線的做法被輿論批為粗暴，也促成後來對西部戰役的檢討；媒體對十歲查理之死的報導引發國會質詢與軍方致歉，顯示遠征軍的紀律與報復心態受到監督。此外，它把西部邊疆「先解決原住民土地問題」的邏輯推到更遠：保留地制度在這幾年裡被視為可行的答案，而莫多克人的下場則被用來證明這套答案的代價。整場戰爭也標誌著美國西部陸軍與遠洋海軍的分工：海軍控制海岸與運輸線，陸軍在內陸山地做攻堅，兩者的技術差距在半個世紀後才被大量推廣的連珠槍與新式後膛砲抹平。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reached far beyond the battlefield. The Modoc ceased to exist as a separate people. The hundred or so left on the reservation were broken up and moved to the Klamath communities inland, while those captured after the break-out and those who surrendered in small numbers were sent to the Quapaw Agency in Indian Territory and mixed with the peoples of Kansas and Oklahoma, and their language and customs were scattered over a few generations; the homeland in the Warner Mountains was absorbed into the national forest. The Klamath suffered with them. After the war they were confined strictly to the reservation, were not to leave without permission, and were required to carry identifying badges, and the area of the reservation was cut back again and again over the following decade and more, the surveyed boundary retreating step by step. In terms of method, this was one of the last of the Indian wars fought in the United States in the pattern of expedition, siege and annihilation; the use of artillery to batter, of engineers to dig saps, and of volunteers placed in the first rank was denounced in the press as brutal, and it prompted a later review of the western campaigns. The press coverage of the death of Ten-year-old Charlie produced questions in Congress and an apology from the army, showing that the discipline and the punitive mood of the expeditions were being watched. In a wider sense the war carried further the western logic of settling the question of Indian land first: the reservation system was treated in these years as a workable answer, and the fate of the Modoc was used to demonstrate the cost of that answer. The war also marks the division of labour between the army in the American West and the navy on the open ocean: the navy held the coast and the lines of transport, the army did the assault work in the interior mountains, and the technological gap between them was not closed until the spread of the Gatling gun and the new breech-loading guns half a century later.
result: 結果是莫多克守軍被逐出堡壘並且被解散。一八七三年四月十一日起的總攻失敗後，圍城繼續，到六月一日，經軍醫埃爾斯沃思往返交涉，莫多克方面同意投降，堡壘內的人隨後被押往後方營地。一八七三年六月六日夜，殘餘數十人趁暴雨衝出堡壘往北逃竄，混戰中十歲查理被斃，老傑克與數人被自己人誤殺，卡普坦·傑克帶著斯克拉洛姆等少數人進入山區，又在三週的追捕中於山路上被擊斃，餘眾或死或降，莫多克作戰單位至此全滅。十月，軍事法庭判處其中三名被俘莫多克死刑並執行，餘部被押往印第安領地安置，保留地方面只留下被迫遷徙的餘民。從戰役層面看，聯邦軍以四個月的圍城、數百人的傷亡與一次引發全國爭議的突圍追殺，換來的是對三百人左右莫多克社群的徹底驅逐；從更大層面看，這一仗是「保留地化」政策的一次示範，也是一次失敗的示範：它證明可以用砲與工兵壓制任何山地堡壘，也證明把一個民族從故地連根拔起，並不會讓邊疆從此安寧。
resultEn: The result was that the Modoc garrison was driven out of the stronghold and the community dissolved. When the assault that began on 11 April 1873 failed, the siege continued, and on 1 June, after the army surgeon Ellsworth had gone back and forth to parley, the Modoc agreed to surrender, and those inside the stronghold were afterwards taken off under escort to the camps in the rear. On the night of 6 June 1873 some dozens of the remnant broke out of the stronghold in a rainstorm and fled north; Ten-year-old Charlie was killed in the fighting, Old Jack and a number of others were shot by their own people by mistake, and Captain Jack with a few followers, Scralom among them, took to the mountains, where after three weeks of pursuit he was killed on a mountain road, the survivors being killed or captured, and the Modoc fighting force came to an end. In October a military commission sentenced three of the captured Modoc to death and the sentence was carried out, and the remainder were removed to Indian Territory; on the reservation only the residue of those forced to move remained. At the level of the operation, the federal army had paid four months of siege, several hundred casualties and a pursuit of a surrendered and fleeing group that raised a controversy across the country, and had won the complete expulsion of a Modoc community of some three hundred people. At the wider level, the war was both a demonstration and a failed demonstration of the reservation policy: it showed that any mountain fortress could be reduced by artillery and engineers, and it showed too that uprooting a people from its homeland did not leave the frontier peaceful afterwards.
